name: TIME
description: TIME builds a time-of-day serial as a decimal fraction of a 24-hour day (0 to 0.999988) from hour, minute, and second components, rolling over values that exceed their normal ranges.
tldr: Converts hour, minute, and second into a time fraction of a day.

parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: The hour component, 0-23. Values of 24 or more roll over into whole days, keeping only the remainder (24 becomes 0, 25 becomes 1).

parameters.name: minute
parameters.description: The minute component, 0-59. Values of 60 or more roll over into hours.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: The second component, 0-59. Values of 60 or more roll over into minutes.

basicExample.explanation: 12 hours is exactly half of a 24-hour day, so TIME returns the fraction 0.5.

advancedExamples.title: Hour overflow drops the day
advancedExamples.description: Hours of 24+ wrap and discard the extra day
advancedExamples.explanation: 25 hours = 1 day and 1 hour; the day is dropped, leaving 1 hour = 1/24 approximately 0.0416667.

advancedExamples.title: Minute overflow rolls into hours
advancedExamples.description: Minutes beyond 59 carry into the hour

howItWorks: TIME converts the three integer inputs into the fraction of a day they represent (hour/24 + minute/1440 + second/86400). It first rolls over out-of-range components, seconds into minutes, minutes into hours, and hours modulo 24, so the final value always lies between 0 and 1.

howToSteps.name: Apply a time format
howToSteps.text: Format the cell as time so the fraction shows as hh:mm:ss.

howToSteps.name: Combine with a date if needed
howToSteps.text: Add a date serial to anchor the time to a specific day.

limitations: TIME returns only the fractional part of a day; hour values of 24+ discard the whole-day portion.
The result is a fraction and must be time-formatted to display correctly.
It cannot represent a time of exactly 24:00:00 (that wraps back to 0).

commonErrors.cause: The cell is in General number format.
commonErrors.fix: Apply a time number format (e.g. h:mm:ss).
Use MOD or split into date and time if you need the day count as well.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TIME is identical in Google Sheets, returning the same fraction of a day.

faq.question: Why is the result 0.5 for noon?
faq.answer: Excel stores time as a fraction of a day; 12/24 = 0.5.

faq.question: What does TIME(25,0,0) return?
faq.answer: 0.0416667, because 25 hours wraps to 1 hour (the extra day is dropped).

faq.question: Can I combine TIME with a date?
faq.answer: Yes, add a date serial, e.g. =DATE(2024,1,1)+TIME(12,0,0) for 2024-01-01 12:00 PM.
